---
name: directory-structure
description: Locate Gkeyll code and understand solver dependencies when exploring the repository or deciding where new code belongs.
---

# Instructions

* Use when exploring the repository, trying to find something, or deciding where new code belongs.
* Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

# Gkeyll file structure

Gkeyll has four PDE solvers: 
* Moments or fluid solver.
* Vlasov solver.
* Gyrokinetic solver.
* PKPM solver.

Correspondingly, these solvers are organized into four separate folders, and they
share some common functionality in a fifth folder. Gkeyll is mostly organized in:
* core/: functionality common to all solvers.
* moments/: files for the moments solver.
* vlasov/: files for the Vlasov solver.
* gyrokinetic/: files for the gyrokinetic solver.
* pkpm/: files for the PKPM solver.

Note that the four solvers are not independent. They have the following
dependencies:
* moments depends on core.
* vlasov depends on moments.
* gyrokinetic depends on vlasov.
* pkpm depends on gyrokinetic.

Keep lower layers independent of higher layers.

Each of the solvers' folders have the sub-folders:
* ker/: C kernels generated with Maxima stored in the gkylcas repository. Do
  not hand-edit generated kernels; modify their source templates instead.
* zero/: C and CUDA functions or modules (sometimes we call them updaters),
  some of which call kernels in ker/.
* data/: data needed for some simulations.
* unit/: unit tests of specific components in zero/.
* apps/: apps are called by input files or regression tests, and they organize
  solver workflow or simulations and call modules in zero/. Communication
  happens in the app level.
* creg/: C regression tests or short simulations to ensure solvers work (these
  are also examples of C input files).
* luareg/: Lua regression tests or short simulations to ensure solvers work
  (these are also examples of Lua input files).

## Library dependencies

The Gkeyll source code in gkeyll/ depends on other libraries installed in gkylsoft/.
Most of the time you shouldn't need to read files in gkylsoft/ unless prompted.

## CPU - GPU organization

Gkeyll runs on both CPUs and GPUs, the latter using CUDA.
- CPU-only implementations live in .c files.
- C files call host-side wrappers of CUDA kernels, both of which live in _cu.cu
  files.

## Search hierarchy

Rather than looking into the entire codebase without prior knowledge, look into
folders in the following order:
- Look into a folder (ending in /) the user referenced.
- If the user referenced a specific solver (e.g. gyrokinetic), look into its
  folder.
- Look into folders for solvers that the specified solver depends on, following
  the dependency chain up through core/.
---
name: compiling
description: How to compile Gkeyll libraries, executables, and specific unit or regression test targets on CPU or CUDA.
---

# Instructions

Use this skill whenever you need to compile
* Any of the Gkeyll libraries.
* A C unit or regression test.
* A C input file.

# Compiling in Gkeyll

We assume the dependencies have already been installed (e.g. via a machines/mkdeps
file) and configured (e.g. via a machines/configure file).

Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).
Dependencies are typically already installed in the sibling `gkylsoft/`
directory. Check the existing configuration before building. If configuration
is missing or needs changing, consult `machines/configure.<machine>.sh` for
required modules and library paths, or use `./configure` with the intended
installation prefix and solver.

## Compiling the Gkeyll library

We compile using a Makefile. The `make` command allows you to specify the number
of cores to use via `-j`. We will use no more than half the available processors for parallel builds.
So before invoking `make`, set the `NPROC` environment variable on a Mac using
```
export NPROC=$(sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu)
NPROC=$((NPROC > 1 ? NPROC / 2 : 1))
```
or on Linux using

```sh
NPROC=$(nproc)
NPROC=$((NPROC > 1 ? NPROC / 2 : 1))
```

Then, you can build the Gkeyll library with

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" install
```

## Compiling a C unit or regression test

Unit tests are located in the `unit/` directory of each solver
(core/moments/vlasov/gyrokinetic/pkpm), while C regression tests are located in `creg/` folders and
have names beginning with `rt_`.

Compile a specific test by giving make its executable target:

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" build/core/unit/ctest_array
make -j"$NPROC" build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1
```

CPU targets are located in `build/`, and  GPU targets are in `cuda-build/`.
Match test targets to the configured build directory.

For executing the resulting tests, see
[testing-and-verification](../testing-and-verification/SKILL.md).

### Compiling all or groups of C unit tests

The Makefile supports compiling groups of unit tests all at once. For example, to compile all the
unit tests at once run

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" unit
```

Alternatively, you can compile all the unit tests for a specific solver. For example, to compile all
the unit tests for the gyrokinetic solver use

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" gyrokinetic-unit
```

## Compiling C input files

Input files written in C work just like C regression tests. They can be compiled similarly if they
are located in the `creg/` folder. For example, if `my_sim.c` is a gyrokinetic input file, and located
in `gyrokinetic/creg/`, it can be compiled with

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" build/gyrokinetic/creg/my_sim
```

If the input file is outside of the repository, use the shared makefile in
`<gkeyll_install_prefix>/share/`. Run it from the directory containing the input
file:

```sh
cd <input_file_directory>
cp <gkeyll_install_prefix>/share/Makefile ./
make
```
---
name: testing-and-verification
description: How to run Gkeyll unit and regression tests, as well as performing memory checks. Use when testing changes and verifying that changes didn't break the code or change simulation results.
---

# Instructions

* For code changes, run relevant unit tests and focused regression tests when
  simulation behavior is affected. Choose tests based on the changed component.
* Do not run the entire regression suite unless you are asked to; it can take a long time.
  Use the task's scope and available resources to choose the suitable testing scope.
* For documentation or agent configuration changes, validate the changed files
  and references; solver tests and memory checks are unnecessary.
* Report what was checked and any checks that could not run. If required context
  is missing or unreadable, report the exact path rather than silently skipping it.

# Running unit tests

Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

In order to run all Gkeyll unit tests:
1. Compile all unit tests; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run all unit tests with
```sh
make -j"$NPROC" unit-run
```

In order to run all unit tests for a specific solver, e.g. gyrokinetic:
1. Compile all unit tests for that solver; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run all unit tests for that solver, e.g. for gyrokinetic use
```sh
make -j"$NPROC" gyrokinetic-unit-run
```

One can also compile and run a single unit test of interest. Simply:
1. Compile the unit; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run the executable from the repository root:
For example, in order to run `core/unit/ctest_array.c` do

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" ./build/core/unit/ctest_array
./build/core/unit/ctest_array
```

If the Gkeyll was build on a CPU-only machine or without GPU support, unit tests will simply ignore
GPU tests (via pre-processor if-statements). When running on a machine with a supported GPU, and if
Gkeyll is configured to build GPU code, running these tests will automatically run the corresponding
GPU tests. If a GPU is not available but Gkeyll was built to use GPUs, the GPU tests may simply fail
or exit (e.g. due to GPU memory allocation errors).

### Parallel unit tests

There are a few parallel unit tests that use MPI, whose names begin with `mctest`. These tests are
compiled the same way as serial tests, but must be run with the appropriate MPI execution command.

For example if Gkeyll was built and configured with the MPI in `gkylsoft/openmpi/`, then a parallel
unit test (for example `mctest_mpi_comm.c`) may be run with

```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 4 build/core/unit/mctest_mpi_comm
```

# Running regression tests

## C regression tests

Regression tests written in C and located in `creg/` directories need to be compiled first,
see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).

Once compiled the regression test may be run serially with, for
`gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1.c` for example:
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1
```

See 
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -h
```
for command line arguments that may be available (not all are actually supported). For
example, the following command
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -s1
```
limits the regression to a one-step smoke test.

CUDA builds place the executable in `cuda-build/` instead of `build/`, and regression tests use `-g`
to indicate GPU execution.

## Parallel regression tests

Regression executables take the `-M` command line argument to indicate a parallel run (requiring
MPI). The flags `-c X -d Y -e Z` specify that the first, second and third configuration-space
dimensions are to be subdivided amongs X, Y and Z MPI processes, respecitively. The product `X*Y*Z`
must match the number of cores available for this run. If one of `-c`, `-d` or `-e` is not given,
it is assumed to be 1.

For example, we may run `gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1` using 2 cores in the second
dimension with
```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -M -d 2
```

For gyrokinetic partition restrictions and an example, read
[gyrokinetic-details](../gyrokinetic-details/SKILL.md).

It is also possible to run with multiple GPUs. Gkeyll's model is to match each MPI process to a
single GPU. The procedure is similar as for multiple GPUs, but the additional `-g` flag is needed.
For example, to run `gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1` using 2 GPUs in the second dimension
with
```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -g -M -d 2
```

## Lua regression tests

Run Lua inputs using the installed executable:

```sh
<gkeyll_install_prefix>/bin/gkeyll <Lua_input_file>
```

## The runregression tool

After installing the Gkeyll library and executable one may use the `runregression` tool to run
regression tests, see

```sh
<gkeyll_install_prefix>/bin/gkeyll runregression -h
```

After configuring runregression, and having generated accepted results with
`runregression run create`, one may check the test using `runregression run check`. Note that the
flag `-r` allows check a specific test or set of tests.

# Memory checks

All code must be free of memory errors and leaks. Run the relevant CPU test
under Valgrind before committing:

```sh
valgrind --leak-check=full ./build/core/unit/ctest_array
```

For GPU changes, run the relevant executable under Compute Sanitizer:

```sh
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --leak-check full <executable>
```

Supply the executable's GPU options where required. Report unavailable tools
or hardware and distinguish completed checks from checks that could not run.

# Gkeyll CI system

Gkeyll has a CI system based on Jenkins which calls the aforementioned existing functionality to run unit and regression tests. See ci/jenkins/README.md for more details.

--- CI guide ---
# Gkeyll Jenkins CI on NERSC Perlmutter GPU

This private, manually triggered CUDA CI builds candidate and baseline CUDA/NCCL
installations on the login node, then submits unit and C-regression work to GPU
nodes. The trusted Pipeline never comes from the candidate PR. CUDA unit tests
run automatically; GPU-capable C regressions are compared with the CUDA/NCCL
baseline built by the Pipeline.
A separate manifest-selected C MPI lane uses four GPU ranks for Vlasov,
gyrokinetic, and PKPM, plus a moments CPU MPI test.

# Installation

## Install Jenkins

Use a controller only in an authenticated Perlmutter session and as permitted
by NERSC policy. Set a project scratch root visible to compute nodes; do not
use `/tmp` or retain durable credentials only there.

An existing Java 21 (or newer) installation is sufficient. To install Java 21
through the NERSC Spack module, use the following once:

```sh
module load spack
spack info openjdk
spack install openjdk@21
```

In each new Perlmutter login session that starts the controller or uses the
Jenkins CLI, load Java and set `JAVA_HOME`:

```sh
module load spack
spack load openjdk@21
export JAVA_HOME="$(spack location --install-dir openjdk@21)"
"$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version
```

`spack install` is needed only once. A controller that has already started in
its detached tmux session continues running after logout, but restarting it or
using the CLI in a later login requires the Java setup above.

```sh
export GKEYLL_CI_ROOT=/pscratch/sd/<first-letter>/<username>/gkeyll_ci
export JAVA_HOME=<java-21-or-newer-installation>
mkdir -p "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT"
java -version
cd "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT"
curl -fL -o jenkins.war https://get.jenkins.io/war-stable/latest/jenkins.war
```

From the reviewed Gkeyll checkout, start the controller (see
`./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh -h`):

```sh
export GKEYLL_CI_ROOT=/pscratch/sd/<first-letter>/<username>/gkeyll_ci
export JAVA_HOME=<java-21-or-newer-installation>
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu start
```

It creates detached tmux session `gkeyll_ci` and binds only to loopback. Use
`tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci` to inspect it or `tmux kill-session -t gkeyll_ci`
to stop it.

Verify the private listener after startup:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/login
ss -ltn | grep '127.0.0.1:8080'
```

## Open Jenkins browser

Jenkins is bound to loopback on the particular Perlmutter login node where its
controller started. In that controller session, record its hostname:

```sh
hostname -f
```

From your laptop, use the public Perlmutter address as a jump host and the
recorded hostname as the final SSH target. For example, if the controller is on
`login20.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov`:

```sh
ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -J <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov \
  -L 127.0.0.1:8084:127.0.0.1:8080 \
  <username>@login20.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov
```

`-f` backgrounds SSH only after authentication and forwarding succeed. Verify
the tunnel from the laptop, then open the local URL:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8084`. The first `8084` is the local browser port; the
final `8080` is the loopback-only Jenkins port on the controller node and
normally remains unchanged. Choose another unused local port if necessary. Do
not use `perlmutter.nersc.gov` as the final SSH target: it can select a
different login node, which produces SSH `channel ... connect failed:
Connection refused` errors. On first start, read
`$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/secrets/initialAdminPassword`, create an admin
account, and install Pipeline, Git, Credentials Binding, Git client, and
GitHub plugins.

## Set up Jenkins

### Create a Jenkins API token for the launcher

Create an API token for the Jenkins user that will launch builds, then save it
on Perlmutter with mode 600:

```sh
umask 077
printf '%s:%s\n' '<jenkins-user>' '<jenkins-api-token>' > "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/jenkins-cli.auth"
chmod 600 "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/jenkins-cli.auth"
```

### Create the GitHub credential

Create a classic GitHub PAT with only the `repo:status` scope and a short
expiration. Its owner must have push access to `gkeyllorg/gkeyll`, which GitHub
requires to publish commit statuses. In **Manage Jenkins → Credentials**, add
it to this controller as a **Username with password** credential: use the
owner's GitHub username and the PAT as the password, then record its ID.
Organization membership is not required.

The Pipeline fetches public candidates anonymously; this PAT is used only for
authenticated GitHub API requests and status publication. Do not share it or
store it outside this controller. Revoke or replace it when the controller or
its owner changes.

### Configure the Jenkins node and global environment

Use a login-side node/agent labelled `perlmutter_gpu`. In **Manage Jenkins →
System → Global properties → Environment variables**, set:

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `GKEYLL_CI_ROOT` | Expanded shared project-scratch root |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ID` | GitHub status/API credential ID |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_SLURM_ACCOUNT` | Required NERSC project/account |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_NODE_LABEL` | Optional; default `perlmutter_gpu` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_SLURM_QOS` | Optional; default `shared` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_BUILD_JOBS` | Optional; default `3` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_UNIT_TIME` | Optional; default `00:30:00` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_TIME` | Optional; default `04:00:00` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_JOBS` | Optional; default `4` |
| `PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_TEST_TIMEOUT` | Optional; default `900` |

### Create the one parameterized Pipeline job

Create **New Item → Pipeline** named `gkeyll-ci-perlmutter_gpu`. Use
**Pipeline script from SCM** with repository `https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll.git`,
no SCM credential, branch `*/main`, and script path
`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu`. The public repository is fetched
anonymously; use node label `perlmutter_gpu`.

Leave **This project is parameterized** unchecked. Click **Build Now** once to
register the Pipeline parameters; its expected empty-selector failure submits
no Slurm job. Do not let a PR supply this Pipeline.

# Launching CI jobs

## CLI launch

```sh
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu run --pr 1234
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu run --candidate-ref feature --baseline-ref main --follow
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu follow --queue 42
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu active
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu info --build 42
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu artifact --build 42 --fetch --only ci-regression-summary.txt
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu abort --build 42
```

## Browser launch

Open the job through the tunnel, select **Build with Parameters**, and set
either `CANDIDATE_PR` or both `CANDIDATE_REF` and `BASELINE_REF`.

# Troubleshooting

## Controller and Slurm jobs

Inspect `tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci`, `$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/logs/jenkins.log`, and
`squeue --me`. After a controller crash, use `scancel <jobid>` before removing
an abandoned workspace.

## Validate manually

Before changing Jenkins, build a disposable main checkout with
`machines/mkdeps.perlmutter.gpu.sh` and `machines/configure.perlmutter.gpu.sh`,
then submit `slurm-unit-tests.perlmutter_gpu.sh` using your account, `shared`
QoS, `--constraint gpu`, 32 CPUs, and one GPU. Build a separate baseline prefix
and compile C regressions in both trees before submitting the regression
Slurm script. This separates NERSC toolchain/allocation failures from Jenkins setup.

name: directory-structure
description: Locate Gkeyll code and understand solver dependencies when exploring the repository or deciding where new code belongs.
---

# Instructions

* Use when exploring the repository, trying to find something, or deciding where new code belongs.
* Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

# Gkeyll file structure

Gkeyll has four PDE solvers: 
* Moments or fluid solver.
* Vlasov solver.
* Gyrokinetic solver.
* PKPM solver.

Correspondingly, these solvers are organized into four separate folders, and they
share some common functionality in a fifth folder. Gkeyll is mostly organized in:
* core/: functionality common to all solvers.
* moments/: files for the moments solver.
* vlasov/: files for the Vlasov solver.
* gyrokinetic/: files for the gyrokinetic solver.
* pkpm/: files for the PKPM solver.

Note that the four solvers are not independent. They have the following
dependencies:
* moments depends on core.
* vlasov depends on moments.
* gyrokinetic depends on vlasov.
* pkpm depends on gyrokinetic.

Keep lower layers independent of higher layers.

Each of the solvers' folders have the sub-folders:
* ker/: C kernels generated with Maxima stored in the gkylcas repository. Do
  not hand-edit generated kernels; modify their source templates instead.
* zero/: C and CUDA functions or modules (sometimes we call them updaters),
  some of which call kernels in ker/.
* data/: data needed for some simulations.
* unit/: unit tests of specific components in zero/.
* apps/: apps are called by input files or regression tests, and they organize
  solver workflow or simulations and call modules in zero/. Communication
  happens in the app level.
* creg/: C regression tests or short simulations to ensure solvers work (these
  are also examples of C input files).
* luareg/: Lua regression tests or short simulations to ensure solvers work
  (these are also examples of Lua input files).

## Library dependencies

The Gkeyll source code in gkeyll/ depends on other libraries installed in gkylsoft/.
Most of the time you shouldn't need to read files in gkylsoft/ unless prompted.

## CPU - GPU organization

Gkeyll runs on both CPUs and GPUs, the latter using CUDA.
- CPU-only implementations live in .c files.
- C files call host-side wrappers of CUDA kernels, both of which live in _cu.cu
  files.

## Search hierarchy

Rather than looking into the entire codebase without prior knowledge, look into
folders in the following order:
- Look into a folder (ending in /) the user referenced.
- If the user referenced a specific solver (e.g. gyrokinetic), look into its
  folder.
- Look into folders for solvers that the specified solver depends on, following
  the dependency chain up through core/.

name: compiling
description: How to compile Gkeyll libraries, executables, and specific unit or regression test targets on CPU or CUDA.
---

# Instructions

Use this skill whenever you need to compile
* Any of the Gkeyll libraries.
* A C unit or regression test.
* A C input file.

# Compiling in Gkeyll

We assume the dependencies have already been installed (e.g. via a machines/mkdeps
file) and configured (e.g. via a machines/configure file).

Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).
Dependencies are typically already installed in the sibling `gkylsoft/`
directory. Check the existing configuration before building. If configuration
is missing or needs changing, consult `machines/configure.<machine>.sh` for
required modules and library paths, or use `./configure` with the intended
installation prefix and solver.

## Compiling the Gkeyll library

We compile using a Makefile. The `make` command allows you to specify the number
of cores to use via `-j`. We will use no more than half the available processors for parallel builds.
So before invoking `make`, set the `NPROC` environment variable on a Mac using
```
export NPROC=$(sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu)
NPROC=$((NPROC > 1 ? NPROC / 2 : 1))
```
or on Linux using

```sh
NPROC=$(nproc)
NPROC=$((NPROC > 1 ? NPROC / 2 : 1))
```

Then, you can build the Gkeyll library with

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" install
```

## Compiling a C unit or regression test

Unit tests are located in the `unit/` directory of each solver
(core/moments/vlasov/gyrokinetic/pkpm), while C regression tests are located in `creg/` folders and
have names beginning with `rt_`.

Compile a specific test by giving make its executable target:

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" build/core/unit/ctest_array
make -j"$NPROC" build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1
```

CPU targets are located in `build/`, and  GPU targets are in `cuda-build/`.
Match test targets to the configured build directory.

For executing the resulting tests, see
[testing-and-verification](../testing-and-verification/SKILL.md).

### Compiling all or groups of C unit tests

The Makefile supports compiling groups of unit tests all at once. For example, to compile all the
unit tests at once run

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" unit
```

Alternatively, you can compile all the unit tests for a specific solver. For example, to compile all
the unit tests for the gyrokinetic solver use

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" gyrokinetic-unit
```

## Compiling C input files

Input files written in C work just like C regression tests. They can be compiled similarly if they
are located in the `creg/` folder. For example, if `my_sim.c` is a gyrokinetic input file, and located
in `gyrokinetic/creg/`, it can be compiled with

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" build/gyrokinetic/creg/my_sim
```

If the input file is outside of the repository, use the shared makefile in
`<gkeyll_install_prefix>/share/`. Run it from the directory containing the input
file:

```sh
cd <input_file_directory>
cp <gkeyll_install_prefix>/share/Makefile ./
make
```

name: testing-and-verification
description: How to run Gkeyll unit and regression tests, as well as performing memory checks. Use when testing changes and verifying that changes didn't break the code or change simulation results.
---

# Instructions

* For code changes, run relevant unit tests and focused regression tests when
  simulation behavior is affected. Choose tests based on the changed component.
* Do not run the entire regression suite unless you are asked to; it can take a long time.
  Use the task's scope and available resources to choose the suitable testing scope.
* For documentation or agent configuration changes, validate the changed files
  and references; solver tests and memory checks are unnecessary.
* Report what was checked and any checks that could not run. If required context
  is missing or unreadable, report the exact path rather than silently skipping it.

# Running unit tests

Operate relative to the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

In order to run all Gkeyll unit tests:
1. Compile all unit tests; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run all unit tests with
```sh
make -j"$NPROC" unit-run
```

In order to run all unit tests for a specific solver, e.g. gyrokinetic:
1. Compile all unit tests for that solver; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run all unit tests for that solver, e.g. for gyrokinetic use
```sh
make -j"$NPROC" gyrokinetic-unit-run
```

One can also compile and run a single unit test of interest. Simply:
1. Compile the unit; see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).
2. Run the executable from the repository root:
For example, in order to run `core/unit/ctest_array.c` do

```sh
make -j"$NPROC" ./build/core/unit/ctest_array
./build/core/unit/ctest_array
```

If the Gkeyll was build on a CPU-only machine or without GPU support, unit tests will simply ignore
GPU tests (via pre-processor if-statements). When running on a machine with a supported GPU, and if
Gkeyll is configured to build GPU code, running these tests will automatically run the corresponding
GPU tests. If a GPU is not available but Gkeyll was built to use GPUs, the GPU tests may simply fail
or exit (e.g. due to GPU memory allocation errors).

### Parallel unit tests

There are a few parallel unit tests that use MPI, whose names begin with `mctest`. These tests are
compiled the same way as serial tests, but must be run with the appropriate MPI execution command.

For example if Gkeyll was built and configured with the MPI in `gkylsoft/openmpi/`, then a parallel
unit test (for example `mctest_mpi_comm.c`) may be run with

```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 4 build/core/unit/mctest_mpi_comm
```

# Running regression tests

## C regression tests

Regression tests written in C and located in `creg/` directories need to be compiled first,
see [compilation](../compiling/SKILL.md).

Once compiled the regression test may be run serially with, for
`gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1.c` for example:
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1
```

See 
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -h
```
for command line arguments that may be available (not all are actually supported). For
example, the following command
```sh
./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -s1
```
limits the regression to a one-step smoke test.

CUDA builds place the executable in `cuda-build/` instead of `build/`, and regression tests use `-g`
to indicate GPU execution.

## Parallel regression tests

Regression executables take the `-M` command line argument to indicate a parallel run (requiring
MPI). The flags `-c X -d Y -e Z` specify that the first, second and third configuration-space
dimensions are to be subdivided amongs X, Y and Z MPI processes, respecitively. The product `X*Y*Z`
must match the number of cores available for this run. If one of `-c`, `-d` or `-e` is not given,
it is assumed to be 1.

For example, we may run `gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1` using 2 cores in the second
dimension with
```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -M -d 2
```

For gyrokinetic partition restrictions and an example, read
[gyrokinetic-details](../gyrokinetic-details/SKILL.md).

It is also possible to run with multiple GPUs. Gkeyll's model is to match each MPI process to a
single GPU. The procedure is similar as for multiple GPUs, but the additional `-g` flag is needed.
For example, to run `gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1` using 2 GPUs in the second dimension
with
```sh
<mpi_install_prefix>/bin/mpirun -np 2 ./build/gyrokinetic/creg/rt_gk_sheath_2x2v_p1 -g -M -d 2
```

## Lua regression tests

Run Lua inputs using the installed executable:

```sh
<gkeyll_install_prefix>/bin/gkeyll <Lua_input_file>
```

## The runregression tool

After installing the Gkeyll library and executable one may use the `runregression` tool to run
regression tests, see

```sh
<gkeyll_install_prefix>/bin/gkeyll runregression -h
```

After configuring runregression, and having generated accepted results with
`runregression run create`, one may check the test using `runregression run check`. Note that the
flag `-r` allows check a specific test or set of tests.

# Memory checks

All code must be free of memory errors and leaks. Run the relevant CPU test
under Valgrind before committing:

```sh
valgrind --leak-check=full ./build/core/unit/ctest_array
```

For GPU changes, run the relevant executable under Compute Sanitizer:

```sh
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --leak-check full <executable>
```

Supply the executable's GPU options where required. Report unavailable tools
or hardware and distinguish completed checks from checks that could not run.

# Gkeyll CI system

Gkeyll has a CI system based on Jenkins which calls the aforementioned existing functionality to run unit and regression tests. See ci/jenkins/README.md for more details.

--- CI guide ---
# Gkeyll Jenkins CI on NERSC Perlmutter GPU

This private, manually triggered CUDA CI builds candidate and baseline CUDA/NCCL
installations on the login node, then submits unit and C-regression work to GPU
nodes. The trusted Pipeline never comes from the candidate PR. CUDA unit tests
run automatically; GPU-capable C regressions are compared with the CUDA/NCCL
baseline built by the Pipeline.
A separate manifest-selected C MPI lane uses four GPU ranks for Vlasov,
gyrokinetic, and PKPM, plus a moments CPU MPI test.

# Installation

## Install Jenkins

Use a controller only in an authenticated Perlmutter session and as permitted
by NERSC policy. Set a project scratch root visible to compute nodes; do not
use `/tmp` or retain durable credentials only there.

An existing Java 21 (or newer) installation is sufficient. To install Java 21
through the NERSC Spack module, use the following once:

```sh
module load spack
spack info openjdk
spack install openjdk@21
```

In each new Perlmutter login session that starts the controller or uses the
Jenkins CLI, load Java and set `JAVA_HOME`:

```sh
module load spack
spack load openjdk@21
export JAVA_HOME="$(spack location --install-dir openjdk@21)"
"$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version
```

`spack install` is needed only once. A controller that has already started in
its detached tmux session continues running after logout, but restarting it or
using the CLI in a later login requires the Java setup above.

```sh
export GKEYLL_CI_ROOT=/pscratch/sd/<first-letter>/<username>/gkeyll_ci
export JAVA_HOME=<java-21-or-newer-installation>
mkdir -p "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT"
java -version
cd "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT"
curl -fL -o jenkins.war https://get.jenkins.io/war-stable/latest/jenkins.war
```

From the reviewed Gkeyll checkout, start the controller (see
`./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh -h`):

```sh
export GKEYLL_CI_ROOT=/pscratch/sd/<first-letter>/<username>/gkeyll_ci
export JAVA_HOME=<java-21-or-newer-installation>
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu start
```

It creates detached tmux session `gkeyll_ci` and binds only to loopback. Use
`tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci` to inspect it or `tmux kill-session -t gkeyll_ci`
to stop it.

Verify the private listener after startup:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/login
ss -ltn | grep '127.0.0.1:8080'
```

## Open Jenkins browser

Jenkins is bound to loopback on the particular Perlmutter login node where its
controller started. In that controller session, record its hostname:

```sh
hostname -f
```

From your laptop, use the public Perlmutter address as a jump host and the
recorded hostname as the final SSH target. For example, if the controller is on
`login20.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov`:

```sh
ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -J <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov \
  -L 127.0.0.1:8084:127.0.0.1:8080 \
  <username>@login20.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov
```

`-f` backgrounds SSH only after authentication and forwarding succeed. Verify
the tunnel from the laptop, then open the local URL:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8084`. The first `8084` is the local browser port; the
final `8080` is the loopback-only Jenkins port on the controller node and
normally remains unchanged. Choose another unused local port if necessary. Do
not use `perlmutter.nersc.gov` as the final SSH target: it can select a
different login node, which produces SSH `channel ... connect failed:
Connection refused` errors. On first start, read
`$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/secrets/initialAdminPassword`, create an admin
account, and install Pipeline, Git, Credentials Binding, Git client, and
GitHub plugins.

## Set up Jenkins

### Create a Jenkins API token for the launcher

Create an API token for the Jenkins user that will launch builds, then save it
on Perlmutter with mode 600:

```sh
umask 077
printf '%s:%s\n' '<jenkins-user>' '<jenkins-api-token>' > "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/jenkins-cli.auth"
chmod 600 "$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/jenkins_home/jenkins-cli.auth"
```

### Create the GitHub credential

Create a classic GitHub PAT with only the `repo:status` scope and a short
expiration. Its owner must have push access to `gkeyllorg/gkeyll`, which GitHub
requires to publish commit statuses. In **Manage Jenkins → Credentials**, add
it to this controller as a **Username with password** credential: use the
owner's GitHub username and the PAT as the password, then record its ID.
Organization membership is not required.

The Pipeline fetches public candidates anonymously; this PAT is used only for
authenticated GitHub API requests and status publication. Do not share it or
store it outside this controller. Revoke or replace it when the controller or
its owner changes.

### Configure the Jenkins node and global environment

Use a login-side node/agent labelled `perlmutter_gpu`. In **Manage Jenkins →
System → Global properties → Environment variables**, set:

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `GKEYLL_CI_ROOT` | Expanded shared project-scratch root |

### Create the one parameterized Pipeline job

Create **New Item → Pipeline** named `gkeyll-ci-perlmutter_gpu`. Use
**Pipeline script from SCM** with repository `https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll.git`,
no SCM credential, branch `*/main`, and script path
`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu`. The public repository is fetched
anonymously; use node label `perlmutter_gpu`.

Leave **This project is parameterized** unchecked. Click **Build Now** once to
register the Pipeline parameters; its expected empty-selector failure submits
no Slurm job. Do not let a PR supply this Pipeline.

# Launching CI jobs

## CLI launch

```sh
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu run --pr 1234
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu run --candidate-ref feature --baseline-ref main --follow
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu follow --queue 42
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu active
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu info --build 42
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu artifact --build 42 --fetch --only ci-regression-summary.txt
./ci/jenkins/gkeyll-ci.sh perlmutter_gpu abort --build 42
```

## Browser launch

Open the job through the tunnel, select **Build with Parameters**, and set
either `CANDIDATE_PR` or both `CANDIDATE_REF` and `BASELINE_REF`.

# Troubleshooting

## Controller and Slurm jobs

Inspect `tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci`, `$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/logs/jenkins.log`, and
`squeue --me`. After a controller crash, use `scancel <jobid>` before removing
an abandoned workspace.

## Validate manually

Before changing Jenkins, build a disposable main checkout with
`machines/mkdeps.perlmutter.gpu.sh` and `machines/configure.perlmutter.gpu.sh`,
then submit `slurm-unit-tests.perlmutter_gpu.sh` using your account, `shared`
QoS, `--constraint gpu`, 32 CPUs, and one GPU. Build a separate baseline prefix
and compile C regressions in both trees before submitting the regression
Slurm script. This separates NERSC toolchain/allocation failures from Jenkins setup.

ea4b46128 Change description in -h menu to clearly mention the console for the 'follow' command
7ee356750 Fix unraveling of CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS env variable in stellar CI.

15473416e Clean up a couple of inconsistencies in docs and variable handling.
8a6450bde For ease of browsing the reason a build failed and getting other stats, add an `info` command to gkeyll-ci/jeci. Amongst other things it prints the list of available artifacts, which can separately be downloaded with the `artifacts` comand.
4be1dd405 Change how team workstation is set up to improve security.
618924c25 Add granularity to stage timing in Jenkins CI. I looked into making something like a 50% runtime increase a reason to fail CI, but realized that there are lots of caveats that make this a bad reason to fail CI. Maybe in a dedicated workstation this will be more reasonable. But I did realized that the timings needed to be more granular, so we do that here.
cd05dd776 Change runregression model a bit so it only does cpu_serial and/or cpu_parallel, OR gpu_serial and/or gpu_parallel. Remove GPU vs CPU comparisons for simplicity (we'll bring that back later). Clean up error codes from runregression, to make querydb more powerful.
3290465f8 Change handling of Jenkins authorization/key file in personal and team workstations to remove one environment variable that was not persistent.
4791daa2e Add a very, very thin Lua wrapper to gkeyll-ci and register it as a Tool for the gkeyll exec (called jeci).

// Manual Level-1 CUDA CI for NERSC's Perlmutter GPU cluster.
//
// Configure the Jenkins job to load *this file* from a reviewed, trusted CI
// branch while Level 1 is being brought up. The PR checkout below is
// intentionally separate: a pull request must not be able to replace the
// pipeline that decides what SLURM work to submit. Once validated, the job can
// move to main without changing this file.

properties([
    buildDiscarder(logRotator(
        numToKeepStr: '20',
        artifactNumToKeepStr: '20'
    )),
    disableConcurrentBuilds(),
    parameters([
        string(
            name: 'CANDIDATE_PR',
            defaultValue: '',
            trim: true,
            description: 'GitHub pull-request number. Set exactly one of CANDIDATE_PR or CANDIDATE_REF.'
        ),
        string(
            name: 'CANDIDATE_REF',
            defaultValue: '',
            trim: true,
            description: 'Candidate branch name or full 40-character commit SHA. Requires BASELINE_REF.'
        ),
        string(
            name: 'BASELINE_REF',
            defaultValue: '',
            trim: true,
            description: 'Baseline branch name or full 40-character commit SHA for CANDIDATE_REF runs.'
        )
    ])
])

def requireValue(String name, String value) {
    value = value?.trim()
    if (!value) {
        error("${name} is not configured. See ci/jenkins/README.perlmutter_gpu.md.")
    }
    return value
}

def buildJobs() {
    def value = (env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_BUILD_JOBS ?: '3').trim()
    return positiveInteger('PERLMUTTER_GPU_BUILD_JOBS', value)
}

def positiveInteger(String name, String value) {
    if (!(value ==~ /[1-9][0-9]*/)) {
        error("${name} must be a positive integer, got '${value}'.")
    }
    return value
}

def regressionJobs() {
    return positiveInteger(
        'PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_JOBS',
        (env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_JOBS ?: '4').trim()
    )
}

def regressionTestTimeout() {
    return positiveInteger(
        'PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_TEST_TIMEOUT',
        (env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_REGRESSION_TEST_TIMEOUT ?: '900').trim()
    )
}

def isCommitSha(String value) {
    return value ==~ /[0-9a-fA-F]{40}/
}

def validateBranchName(String name, String value) {
    if (!(value ==~ /[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\/-]*/)
        || value.contains('..') || value.contains('//')
        || value.endsWith('/') || value.endsWith('.') || value.endsWith('.lock')) {
        error("${name} must be a safe branch name or a full 40-character commit SHA, got '${value}'.")
    }
    return value
}

def validateRefSelector(String name, String value) {
    value = requireValue(name, value)
    return isCommitSha(value) ? value.toLowerCase() : validateBranchName(name, value)
}

def checkoutPullRequest(String prNumber) {
    checkout([
        $class: 'GitSCM',
        branches: [[name: "refs/remotes/origin/candidate"]],
        doGenerateSubmoduleConfigurations: false,
        extensions: [
            [$class: 'CleanBeforeCheckout'],
            [$class: 'CloneOption', depth: 1, honorRefspec: true, noTags: true, shallow: true]
        ],
        userRemoteConfigs: [[
            refspec: "+refs/pull/${prNumber}/head:refs/remotes/origin/candidate",
            url: 'https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll.git'
        ]]
    ])
}

def checkoutRef(String selector, String localRef) {
    def refspec = isCommitSha(selector)
        ? "+${selector}:refs/remotes/origin/${localRef}"
        : "+refs/heads/${selector}:refs/remotes/origin/${localRef}"
    checkout([
        $class: 'GitSCM',
        branches: [[name: "refs/remotes/origin/${localRef}"]],
        doGenerateSubmoduleConfigurations: false,
        extensions: [
            [$class: 'CleanBeforeCheckout'],
            [$class: 'CloneOption', depth: 1, honorRefspec: true, noTags: true, shallow: true]
        ],
        userRemoteConfigs: [[
            refspec: refspec,
            url: 'https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll.git'
        ]]
    ])
}

def resolvePullRequestBase(String statusCredentialsId, String prNumber) {
    def baseRef = ''
    withCredentials([usernamePassword(
        credentialsId: statusCredentialsId,
        usernameVariable: 'GITHUB_STATUS_USERNAME',
        passwordVariable: 'GITHUB_STATUS_TOKEN'
    )]) {
        withEnv(["GITHUB_PR_NUMBER=${prNumber}"]) {
            baseRef = sh(returnStdout: true, script: '''#!/bin/bash
                set -euo pipefail
                curl --fail --silent --show-error \
                    --retry 2 --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 45 \
                    --header 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
                    --header 'X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28' \
                    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_STATUS_TOKEN}" \
                    "https://api.github.com/repos/gkeyllorg/gkeyll/pulls/${GITHUB_PR_NUMBER}" \
                    | python3 -c '
import json
import sys

pull = json.load(sys.stdin)
base_ref = (pull.get("base") or {}).get("ref") or ""
if not isinstance(base_ref, str):
    raise SystemExit("GitHub pull-request base ref is not a string")
print(base_ref)
'
            ''').trim()
        }
    }
    return validateBranchName('GitHub PR base branch', baseRef)
}

def publishGitHubCommitStatus(String statusCredentialsId, String commit, String state, String description) {
    if (!(commit ==~ /[0-9a-f]{40}/)) {
        error("Cannot publish a GitHub status for invalid commit SHA '${commit}'.")
    }
    if (!['pending', 'success', 'failure', 'error'].contains(state)) {
        error("Invalid GitHub commit-status state '${state}'.")
    }

    // Bind the token only for this trusted API request, never while a shell
    // command from the PR checkout is running.
    withCredentials([usernamePassword(
        credentialsId: statusCredentialsId,
        usernameVariable: 'GITHUB_STATUS_USERNAME',
        passwordVariable: 'GITHUB_STATUS_TOKEN'
    )]) {
        withEnv([
            "GITHUB_STATUS_COMMIT=${commit}",
            "GITHUB_STATUS_STATE=${state}",
            "GITHUB_STATUS_DESCRIPTION=${description}"
        ]) {
            sh '''#!/bin/bash
                set -euo pipefail

                payload="$(printf '{"state":"%s","context":"continuous-integration/jenkins/perlmutter_gpu","description":"%s"}' "${GITHUB_STATUS_STATE}" "${GITHUB_STATUS_DESCRIPTION}")"
                curl --fail --silent --show-error \
                    --retry 2 --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 45 \
                    --request POST \
                    --header 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
                    --header 'X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28' \
                    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_STATUS_TOKEN}" \
                    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                    --data "$payload" \
                    --output /dev/null --write-out 'GitHub Perlmutter status: %{http_code}\\n' \
                    "https://api.github.com/repos/gkeyllorg/gkeyll/statuses/${GITHUB_STATUS_COMMIT}"
            '''
        }
    }
}

def submitSlurmJob(String kind, String payload, String timeLimit, List<String> extraExports = [], String tasks = '1', String cpus = '32', String gpus = '1') {
    def qos = (env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_SLURM_QOS ?: 'shared').trim()
    def account = requireValue('PERLMUTTER_GPU_SLURM_ACCOUNT', env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_SLURM_ACCOUNT)
    def idFile = "slurm-${kind}-job-id.txt"
    def statusFile = "slurm-${kind}-job-status.txt"
    def outputFile = "slurm-${kind}-%j.out"
    def exports = [
        "CI_WORKSPACE=${env.WORKSPACE}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND=${kind}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_ID_FILE=${idFile}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_STATUS_FILE=${statusFile}"
    ] + extraExports

    withEnv([
        "CI_WORKSPACE=${env.WORKSPACE}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND=${kind}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_ID_FILE=${idFile}",
        "CI_SLURM_JOB_STATUS_FILE=${statusFile}",
        "CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_QOS=${qos}",
        "CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_TIME=${timeLimit}",
        "CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_ACCOUNT=${account}",
        "CI_SLURM_TASKS=${tasks}",
        "CI_SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK=${cpus}",
        "CI_SLURM_GPUS_PER_TASK=${gpus}",
        "CI_SLURM_PAYLOAD=${payload}",
        "CI_SLURM_EXPORTS=${exports.join(',')}",
        "CI_SLURM_OUTPUT=${outputFile}"
    ]) {
        sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
            set -euo pipefail

            job_id=''

            write_status() {
                printf 'job_id=%s\nstate=%s\nexit_code=%s\nelapsed_seconds=%s\n' \
                    "$job_id" "$1" "${2:-}" "${3:-}" > "$CI_SLURM_JOB_STATUS_FILE"
            }

            cancel_submitted_job() {
                trap - INT TERM
                if [[ -z "$job_id" ]]; then
                    exit 143
                fi

                echo "Jenkins interrupted; cancelling Slurm job $job_id"
                scancel "$job_id" || true
                while :; do
                    state="$(squeue --noheader --jobs="$job_id" --format='%T' | head -n 1 || true)"
                    if [[ -z "$state" ]]; then
                        break
                    fi
                    echo "Waiting for Slurm job $job_id to stop (state: $state)"
                    sleep 5
                done
                write_status 'CANCELLED_BY_JENKINS'
                exit 143
            }

            trap cancel_submitted_job INT TERM

            sbatch_args=(
                --parsable
                "--job-name=gkyl-ci-${CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND}-${BUILD_NUMBER}"
                --nodes=1
                "--ntasks=${CI_SLURM_TASKS}"
                --constraint=gpu
                "--cpus-per-task=${CI_SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}"
                "--gpus-per-task=${CI_SLURM_GPUS_PER_TASK}"
                "--qos=${CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_QOS}"
                "--time=${CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_TIME}"
                "--output=${CI_WORKSPACE}/${CI_SLURM_OUTPUT}"
                "--chdir=${CI_WORKSPACE}"
                "--export=ALL,${CI_SLURM_EXPORTS}"
            )
            sbatch_args+=("--account=${CI_PERLMUTTER_GPU_ACCOUNT}")

            submission="$(sbatch "${sbatch_args[@]}" "$CI_SLURM_PAYLOAD")"
            job_id="${submission%%;*}"
            if [[ ! "$job_id" =~ ^[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
                echo "ERROR: Could not parse Slurm job ID from: $submission" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "$job_id" > "$CI_SLURM_JOB_ID_FILE"
            echo "Submitted ${CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND} Slurm job $job_id"

            previous_state=''
            while :; do
                state="$(squeue --noheader --jobs="$job_id" --format='%T' | head -n 1 || true)"
                if [[ -z "$state" ]]; then
                    break
                fi
                if [[ "$state" != "$previous_state" ]]; then
                    echo "${CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND} Slurm job $job_id state: $state"
                    previous_state="$state"
                fi
                sleep 5
            done

            # Slurm accounting can lag briefly after a job disappears from
            # squeue. Query the allocation record only (-X) until it appears.
            record=''
            for attempt in {1..6}; do
                record="$(sacct --noheader --parsable2 --allocations --jobs="$job_id" \
                    --format=State,ExitCode,ElapsedRaw | head -n 1 || true)"
                if [[ -n "$record" ]]; then
                    break
                fi
                echo "Waiting for Slurm accounting record for job $job_id ($attempt/6)"
                sleep 5
            done
            if [[ -z "$record" ]]; then
                write_status 'UNKNOWN'
                echo "ERROR: No Slurm accounting record found for job $job_id" >&2
                exit 1
            fi

            IFS='|' read -r final_state exit_code elapsed_seconds <<< "$record"
            write_status "$final_state" "$exit_code" "$elapsed_seconds"
            echo "${CI_SLURM_JOB_KIND} Slurm job $job_id finished: state=$final_state exit_code=$exit_code elapsed_seconds=$elapsed_seconds"
            if [[ "$final_state" == COMPLETED* && "$exit_code" == '0:0' ]]; then
                exit 0
            fi
            exit 1
        '''
    }
}

def configureAndCompileCRegressions(String label, String driver, String sourceDir, String prefix, String moduleFile, String runOptions = '', String configureOptions = '') {
    withEnv([
        "CI_REGRESSION_LABEL=${label}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER=${driver}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_SOURCE_DIR=${sourceDir}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_PREFIX=${prefix}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_MODULE_FILE=${moduleFile}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS=${runOptions}",
        "CI_REGRESSION_CONFIGURE_OPTIONS=${configureOptions}"
    ]) {
        sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
            set -euo pipefail
            . "$CI_REGRESSION_MODULE_FILE"
            "$CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER" runregression configure \
                --source-dir "$CI_REGRESSION_SOURCE_DIR" \
                --prefix "$CI_REGRESSION_PREFIX" ${CI_REGRESSION_CONFIGURE_OPTIONS:-}
            started="$(date +%s)"
            "$CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER" runregression run -c $CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS compile
            elapsed="$(( $(date +%s) - started ))"
            printf '%s\n' "$elapsed" > "$CI_REGRESSION_LABEL-c-compile-seconds.txt"
            echo "$CI_REGRESSION_LABEL C-regression compile time: $elapsed seconds"
        '''
    }
}

def finalizeUnfinishedSlurmJob() {
    // Jenkins may terminate a durable-task process tree before its shell trap
    // completes. Run this from the Pipeline finally block as a second chance
    // to cancel a submitted job and preserve an abort-status artifact.
    sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
        set -euo pipefail

        for id_file in slurm-*-job-id.txt; do
            [[ -e "$id_file" ]] || continue
            status_file="${id_file%-id.txt}-status.txt"
            [[ -e "$status_file" ]] && continue

            job_id="$(<"$id_file")"
            if [[ ! "$job_id" =~ ^[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
                printf 'job_id=%s\nstate=UNKNOWN\nexit_code=\n' "$job_id" > "$status_file"
                echo "WARNING: Cannot cancel malformed Slurm job ID '$job_id'" >&2
                continue
            fi

            echo "Pipeline finalizer: cancelling unfinished Slurm job $job_id"
            scancel "$job_id" || true
            while :; do
                state="$(squeue --noheader --jobs="$job_id" --format='%T' | head -n 1 || true)"
                if [[ -z "$state" ]]; then
                    break
                fi
                echo "Pipeline finalizer: waiting for job $job_id to stop (state: $state)"
                sleep 5
            done
            printf 'job_id=%s\nstate=CANCELLED_BY_JENKINS\nexit_code=\n' "$job_id" > "$status_file"
        done
    '''
}

def writeCiTimingSummary() {
    sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
        set -euo pipefail

        metric() {
            local file="$1"
            local key="$2"
            if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
                local value
                if [[ "$key" == '__file__' ]]; then
                    value="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$file")"
                else
                    value="$(sed -n -E "s/^${key}=//p" "$file" | tail -n 1)"
                fi
                if [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
                    printf '%s' "$value"
                    return
                fi
            fi
            printf 'not-recorded'
        }

        candidate_compile="$(metric candidate-c-compile-seconds.txt __file__)"
        baseline_compile="$(metric baseline-c-compile-seconds.txt __file__)"
        candidate_parallel_compile="$(metric candidate-parallel-c-compile-seconds.txt __file__)"
        baseline_parallel_compile="$(metric baseline-parallel-c-compile-seconds.txt __file__)"
        candidate_install="$(metric candidate-install-seconds.txt __file__)"
        baseline_install="$(metric baseline-install-seconds.txt __file__)"
        candidate_unit_build="$(metric candidate-unit-build-seconds.txt __file__)"
        baseline_unit_build="$(metric baseline-unit-build-seconds.txt __file__)"
        candidate_unit_test="$(metric unit-test-seconds.txt __file__)"
        baseline_unit_test='not-recorded'
        regression_create="$(metric baseline-c-regression-create-seconds.txt __file__)"
        regression_check="$(metric candidate-c-regression-check-seconds.txt __file__)"
        parallel_regression_create="$(metric baseline-parallel-c-regression-create-seconds.txt __file__)"
        parallel_regression_check="$(metric candidate-parallel-c-regression-check-seconds.txt __file__)"
        unit_elapsed="$(metric slurm-unit-job-status.txt elapsed_seconds)"
        regression_elapsed="$(metric slurm-regression-job-status.txt elapsed_seconds)"
        parallel_regression_elapsed="$(metric slurm-parallel-regression-job-status.txt elapsed_seconds)"
        c_passed="$(metric ci-regression-summary.txt c_regression_passed)"
        c_acknowledged="$(metric ci-regression-summary.txt c_regression_acknowledged)"
        c_unacknowledged="$(metric ci-regression-summary.txt c_regression_unacknowledged)"

        compile_total='not-recorded'
        if [[ "$candidate_compile" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$baseline_compile" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            compile_total="$((candidate_compile + baseline_compile))"
        fi

        {
            printf 'candidate_c_compile_seconds=%s\n' "$candidate_compile"
            printf 'baseline_c_compile_seconds=%s\n' "$baseline_compile"
            printf 'candidate_parallel_c_compile_seconds=%s\n' "$candidate_parallel_compile"
            printf 'baseline_parallel_c_compile_seconds=%s\n' "$baseline_parallel_compile"
            printf 'login_c_compile_seconds=%s\n' "$compile_total"
            printf 'candidate_install_seconds=%s\n' "$candidate_install"
            printf 'baseline_install_seconds=%s\n' "$baseline_install"
            printf 'candidate_unit_build_seconds=%s\n' "$candidate_unit_build"
            printf 'baseline_unit_build_seconds=%s\n' "$baseline_unit_build"
            printf 'candidate_unit_test_seconds=%s\n' "$candidate_unit_test"
            printf 'baseline_unit_test_seconds=%s\n' "$baseline_unit_test"
            printf 'baseline_c_regression_create_seconds=%s\n' "$regression_create"
            printf 'candidate_c_regression_check_seconds=%s\n' "$regression_check"
            printf 'baseline_parallel_c_regression_create_seconds=%s\n' "$parallel_regression_create"
            printf 'candidate_parallel_c_regression_check_seconds=%s\n' "$parallel_regression_check"
            printf 'unit_slurm_elapsed_seconds=%s\n' "$unit_elapsed"
            printf 'regression_slurm_elapsed_seconds=%s\n' "$regression_elapsed"
            printf 'parallel_regression_slurm_elapsed_seconds=%s\n' "$parallel_regression_elapsed"
            printf 'c_regression_passed=%s\n' "$c_passed"
            printf 'c_regression_acknowledged=%s\n' "$c_acknowledged"
            printf 'c_regression_unacknowledged=%s\n' "$c_unacknowledged"
        } > ci-timing-summary.txt
        cat ci-timing-summary.txt
    '''
}

def timingMetric(String key) {
    if (!fileExists('ci-timing-summary.txt')) {
        return 'n/a'
    }
    def expression = '(?m)^' + java.util.regex.Pattern.quote(key) + '=([^\\r\\n]+)$'
    def match = readFile('ci-timing-summary.txt') =~ expression
    return match.find() ? match.group(1) : 'n/a'
}

def timingStatusDescription(String status) {
    def passed = timingMetric('c_regression_passed')
    def acknowledged = timingMetric('c_regression_acknowledged')
    def unacknowledged = timingMetric('c_regression_unacknowledged')
    def candidateCompile = timingMetric('candidate_c_compile_seconds')
    def baselineCompile = timingMetric('baseline_c_compile_seconds')
    def unitElapsed = timingMetric('unit_slurm_elapsed_seconds')
    def regressionElapsed = timingMetric('regression_slurm_elapsed_seconds')
    def outcome = status == 'success' ? 'passed' : (status == 'error' ? 'errored' : 'failed')
    def description = "Perlmutter CI ${outcome}: C ${passed}/${acknowledged}/${unacknowledged}; comp C/B ${candidateCompile}/${baselineCompile}s; Slurm U/R ${unitElapsed}/${regressionElapsed}s"
    return description.take(140)
}

def workspaceRoot = "${gkeyllCiRoot}/workspaces"
def statusCredentialsId = requireValue('PERLMUTTER_GPU_GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ID', env.PERLMUTTER_GPU_GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ID)
def candidateSelector = ''
def baselineSelector = ''
def candidateCommit = ''
def terminalStatus = 'failure'
def terminalDescription = 'Perlmutter GPU CI failed.'
def failureMessage = ''

def ciStage(String stageName, Closure body) {
    env.CI_FAILURE_STAGE = stageName
    stage(stageName) { body.call() }
}

def writeCiFailureSummary(String result, String stageName, String message) {
    def compactMessage = (message ?: 'unknown failure').replaceAll('[\\r\\n]+', ' ').trim().take(500)
    writeFile file: 'ci-failure-summary.txt', text: "result=${result}\nstage=${stageName ?: 'unknown'}\nmessage=${compactMessage}\n"
}

node(nodeLabel) {
    // Perlmutter compute nodes must see this path. Configure the root on a shared
    // filesystem such as the project's /scratch/gpfs location, never /tmp.
    ws("${workspaceRoot}/${env.JOB_NAME}/${env.BUILD_TAG}") {
        try {
            ciStage('Resolve candidate and baseline') {
                if (candidatePr) {
                    candidateSelector = "PR #${candidatePr}"
                    baselineSelector = resolvePullRequestBase(statusCredentialsId, candidatePr)
                } else {
                    candidateSelector = candidateRef
                    baselineSelector = requestedBaselineRef
                }
                echo "Candidate selector: ${candidateSelector}"
                echo "Baseline selector: ${baselineSelector}"
            }
            ciStage('Checkout candidate') {
                deleteDir()
                if (candidatePr) {
                    checkoutPullRequest(candidatePr)
                } else {
                    checkoutRef(candidateRef, 'candidate')
                }
                candidateCommit = sh(returnStdout: true, script: 'git rev-parse HEAD').trim()
                writeFile file: 'ci-candidate-commit.txt', text: "${candidateCommit}\n"
                writeFile file: 'ci-selection.txt', text: "candidate_selector=${candidateSelector}\nbaseline_selector=${baselineSelector}\n"
                sh 'git status --short'
            }
            ciStage('Report pending to GitHub') {
                publishGitHubCommitStatus(
                    statusCredentialsId,
                    candidateCommit,
                    'pending',
                    'Perlmutter GPU candidate CI is running.'
                )
            }
            ciStage('Build dependencies') {
                withEnv(["PREFIX=${env.WORKSPACE}/gkylsoft"]) {
                    sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
                        set -euo pipefail
                        ./machines/mkdeps.perlmutter.gpu.sh
                    '''
                }
            }
            ciStage('Configure') {
                withEnv(["PREFIX=${env.WORKSPACE}/gkylsoft"]) {
                    sh '''#!/bin/bash -l
                        set -euo pipefail
                        ./machines/configure.perlmutter.gpu.sh
                    '''
                }
            }
            ciStage('Build unit tests') {
                def jobs = buildJobs()
                sh """#!/bin/bash -l
                    set -euo pipefail
                    # Each Jenkins sh step is a new process, so source the
                    # same environment used by the Perlmutter machine scripts.
                    . machines/module_load.perlmutter-gpu.sh
                    module list
                    started=\$(date +%s)
                    make -j${jobs} unit
                    elapsed=\$(( \$(date +%s) - started ))
                    printf '%s\\n' "\$elapsed" > candidate-unit-build-seconds.txt
                    echo "Candidate unit-test build time: \$elapsed seconds"
                """

# Fix Perlmutter GPU CI regression compilation

## Summary

The run failed before any C regression compiled or any regression Slurm job was submitted. In `Compile candidate C regressions`, Bash’s `set -u` rejected an unset `CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS`:

`CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS: unbound variable`

The default Groovy argument is `''`, but Jenkins does not reliably preserve that as an exported shell variable. The Pipeline then expands it directly.

## Key change

- In `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu`, change the regression compile invocation to:
  ```bash
  "$CI_REGRESSION_DRIVER" runregression run -c ${CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS:-} compile
  ```
- This treats an unset option variable as empty while preserving any future nonempty options.
- Mirror the already-applied fix in `Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu` (commit `7ee356750`).

## Test plan

- Validate the Jenkinsfile shell fragment with `CI_REGRESSION_RUN_OPTIONS` unset under `set -euo pipefail`; it should invoke `runregression run -c compile`.
- Launch a Perlmutter GPU CI run and confirm candidate/baseline regression compilation completes, followed by serial and parallel regression Slurm stages.

## Assumptions

- Empty run options are intentional for the normal Perlmutter candidate and baseline compilation paths.
- The Cray module reload messages are informational; the console shows successful installation and unit-test completion before this deterministic shell failure.
